## 2. S51-1 — the seeded coupons' deterministic display order (LOW, seed determinism)

**Finding:** run 52's screenshot refresh produced a 15b-admin-coupons
raster that differed from the committed run-51 raster by 11,876
pixels (0.63%) in the card-grid region — with the DB verified in the
documented final-capture state (5 orders / 17 reviews / FREESHIP 1)
before and after. A VLM read of both crops isolated the delta: the
**SAVE20 and FREESHIP cards had swapped grid positions**; every
card's content was otherwise identical.

**Root cause:** the seed's coupon loop created its three rows within
~1ms of each other (this run: WELCOME10 .090Z, SAVE20 .091Z,
FREESHIP .091Z — a genuine tie), and `/admin/coupons` lists coupons
`orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }` on SQLite's millisecond-precision
DateTime strings. A same-millisecond tie has no deterministic
tie-break, so the card order flipped run-to-run depending on where
the insert loop's clock ticks landed. The product catalog has been
immune to this class since session-12 (`productSeedCreatedAt`'s
60-second backdated spacing); the coupons never got the same
treatment.

**Fix (TDD — `tests/unit/session51-hardening.test.ts` written RED
first, 6/6 failing before the implementation):**
1. New pure helper `couponSeedCreatedAt(index, now)` in
   `src/lib/seed-policy.ts` — the coupon twin of
   `productSeedCreatedAt`: the first-listed row is the newest, each
   successor backdated a full 60 seconds (no tie possible at SQLite's
   ms precision), non-negative-integer index guard.
2. `prisma/seed.ts`: the COUPONS array reordered into the admin
   DISPLAY order (FREESHIP → SAVE20 → WELCOME10 — the card order the
   page has shipped since session-19 and that the 15b screenshot
   pins) and now EXPORTED (the PRODUCTS precedent); the coupon
   upsert's create branch carries
   `createdAt: couponSeedCreatedAt(index)` while `update: {}` stays
   create-only — existing databases keep their own timestamps and
   redemption bookkeeping untouched (the S4-8/S7-3 policy), and
   admin-created coupons still sort as the newest via their real
   `now()`.
3. The unit pins: the helper's strictly-descending/60s-gap contract
   AND the COUPONS array order + the three seeded lifecycle shapes.

**Verified end-to-end:** fresh wipe → db:setup → the DB's
`createdAt desc` order reads FREESHIP → SAVE20 → WELCOME10 with
distinct 60s-spaced timestamps (.912/.913/.913 across three different
minutes); the full capture sequence (wipe → seed → ONE e2e run →
restore-demo-stock → capture) then reproduced **24/25 byte-identical
screenshots** — 15b back at the committed FREESHIP-first raster
EXACTLY, the only changed shot being 03-product-detail (the
documented traffic-owned Date.now() e2e-review rows).

## 2. Findings → work items

### S53-1 (LOW, capture-tooling) — the full-page screenshot raster can outrun below-fold lazy images

**Evidence**: the first screenshot refresh of the run produced a
`02-products.png` 660,937 pixels (21.1%) different from the committed
run-53 raster against the documented final-capture DB state — two
290px content bands (y736-1025, y1230-1519 = grid rows 2 and 3).
A pure-Node pixel-diff classified both bands CONTENT-level (not the
±1-LSB noise class); VLM reads of both band crops isolated the
semantic delta: **the product photos are present in the committed
raster and BLANK in the new capture, with every text/price/badge/
layout element identical**. All 25 standalone `public/images/` files
exist on disk; the DB image refs are unchanged; the parity grid had
just verified all card content on the live server.

**Root cause**: the `02-products` shot waited only for
`html[data-hydrated="true"]` — NO image gate. The products grid
renders 16 `loading="lazy"` cards; a Playwright `fullPage` screenshot
expands the viewport past every lazy image at once and can rasterize
before the below-fold decodes finish. Run 53 produced a byte-identical
02 only because its images won the race; this run (cold standalone
server, cold OS page cache) lost it on rows 2-3 while rows 1+4 still
won — the exact probabilistic signature of a capture-gate race (the
S35-2 badge race, S37-2 toast race, S42-2 panel-raster race and
S50-1 chart-animation race family, now on the lazy-image surface).

**Fix (TDD-shaped, the RED is the captured failing raster)**:
`scripts/capture-screenshots.mjs` gains `waitForImages(page)` —
promote every `<img>` to `loading="eager"` (per spec, flipping a
not-yet-loaded lazy image to eager starts its load) and gate on
`document.images` being complete with `naturalWidth > 0` (15s
timeout — a genuinely broken image fails the capture loudly instead
of shipping a blank docs raster), plus a 120ms decode-to-raster
settle. Applied inside `shoot()` for `mode === "full"` — ONE
insertion point covering every structurally-exposed full-page shot
(the class lives in fullPage stitching; viewport shots load eagerly).

**Verified end-to-end**: re-ran the full capture after the fix (the
documented 60s login-limiter window respected) — **25/25 green,
`02-products` back at ZERO changed pixels (byte-identical to the
committed raster), and the sole remaining delta `03-product-detail`
at 664 pixels in a single 11px band at y1168-1178 — exactly the
documented traffic-owned Date.now() e2e-review-row class.** RED →
GREEN.

### Environmental (no repo action) — the live reference site is down

Recorded above: HTTP 503 + "publish the app in Builder" on every
probed path, stable across ~3 minutes. The reference parity protocol
ran on the documented pins + the run-53 standing live baseline. If
the reference returns in a future cycle, re-verify live; if it stays
down, the session-34 pin + seed embodiment remain the canonical
expectations (DB-verified each cycle).

## The orphaned-server incident (the cycle's lesson)

The first capture-sequence e2e run dropped to **37/67** with login-flow
`toHaveURL` failures. Root cause (reproduced and verified): the parity-grid
server started earlier in the session SURVIVED its `pkill -f "node
.next/standalone/server.js"` — Next.js renames the standalone server
process to `next-server (v16.4.0)`, so the pattern never matched. The
orphan (parented to init) then served TWO poisoned properties to the e2e
webServer's `reuseExistingServer` path: (1) its SQLite connection still
held the DELETED pre-reseed DB inode — the fresh reseed's `rm db/custom.db`
created a new file, but the orphan kept reading the old one, so the suite
tested against the STALE traffic state (order-number pins broke at
ORD-2026-006+); and (2) its in-memory rate limiter accumulated login
budgets across runs, so the diagnostic re-run's login-dependent specs all
got 429-rejected. The fix: kill by PORT OWNER (`ss -tlnp` → the listening
pid), never by command-line pattern; after the correct kill + fresh
reseed, the single e2e run returned to exactly **67/67 at 1.9m** with the
exact documented traffic class. The signature for this class going
forward: a gate that drops from 67 to ~37 with login `toHaveURL` failures
while guest-only specs stay green.

### S69-2 (the 404-hydration fix — TDD)

The run-70 parity grid added a branded-404 surface — and its
"zero console errors" gate failed with **16 CSP violations localized
to `/no-such-route-xyz`**: the prerendered `not-found.tsx` shell baked
no per-request nonce into its script tags (the proxy stamps one on
every response), so the browser refused them all — the route never
hydrated (the exact class the (auth) layout documents). No prior
grid/e2e/a11y surface had ever hard-loaded a 404.

Fix: the documented pattern — `await connection()` in
`not-found.tsx` forces per-request rendering of `/_not-found` (the
route table now shows `ƒ /_not-found`; the other 22 static shells
unchanged; build green, zero prisma:error). Pinned TDD-first: the new
seo-platform e2e test ("the branded 404 hydrates on the server") timed
out RED on the pre-fix build; GREEN post-fix. **The e2e suite grew
67 → 68.**

**The mission changed.** The operator's new reference app is
`https://ely-beauty.base44.app/` — a *different* Base44 app from the dead
`nest-culinary-hub` one: a high-fashion, editorial premium-skincare storefront
(BDT ৳, Bangladesh, Cash on Delivery). The repo (renamed `ely-beauty`) was
re-skinned from the HomeNest Kitchen scaffold into the ElyBeauty clone:
visual parity on every reference surface, every hardened superset capability
retained. The run was planned in `docs/implementation-plan.md` and executed
against the live-reference dossier `docs/reference-investigation.md`
(investigated live 2026-11-08, logged in with the operator credentials; one
clearly-named verification order placed — ELY-MW774C50, ৳358 — the operator
may delete it).

### The change-set (commit 42e9d95)

- **Design tokens**: Cormorant Garamond 300–600 + Inter 300–600 (next/font);
  ivory `hsl(30 20% 97%)` / taupe `hsl(30 12% 48%)` / 4px radii; borderless
  editorial product cards; fixed transparent-over-hero header on `/` (solid
  ivory + hairline elsewhere); uppercase micro-labels + underlined text CTAs;
  WhatsApp float; 4-column ivory footer.
- **Catalog**: 19 products / 4 categories seeded from the reference's public
  entity API in its authored order; ৳ integer-cent money (whole-taka
  display); sold-out pieces visible; variant data (colors/sizes) + full
  description/how-to-use/ingredients copy.
- **Commerce**: product variants as cart-line identity
  (`@@unique([cartId, productId, variant])`, empty-string default);
  `OrderItem.variantLabel` snapshots; composite-key merge/bulk planning;
  city-tiered shipping via the pure `shippingMethodForCity` (Dhaka ৳70 /
  outside ৳130, "Enter city to calculate" before input); crypto-random
  `ELY-XXXXXXXX` order numbers; optional `Order.notes`; the BD address model
  (state/ZIP optional, state back-filled from city).
- **Checkout**: the reference's single-page form (CONTACT / SHIPPING ADDRESS /
  PAYMENT METHOD / Order Notes + ORDER SUMMARY with live shipping + coupon
  box) — Cash on Delivery default; the Card option + Payment Element only
  when Stripe is configured. Every invariant kept: server-derived money
  in-tx, idempotency key, scoped cart clear, ownership-bound replay,
  token-gated receipt.
- **Routes**: `/products` → `/shop` (301; sitemap/SEO/JSON-LD follow);
  reference nav (SHOP / BEAUTY TOOLS / BRUSH & COMBS / ABOUT); mobile panel
  with the in-panel SEARCH flow; desktop search overlay; "Your Bag" drawer;
  account lands on ORDER HISTORY; login/register reference copy + the
  disabled Google parity button.
- **Imagery**: 27 independently generated brand images (`scripts/generate-imagery.mjs`)
  — the reference hotlinks a third-party Shopify CDN; no asset laundering.
- **NEW Tailwind v4 trap (the run's find)**: `@apply` cannot reference
  classes declared in `@layer utilities` ("Cannot apply unknown utility
  class") — apply-able custom classes must be declared with `@utility`
  (`eyebrow-label` / `link-cta` in `globals.css`). Logged in AGENTS.md trap
  6 and the SKILL.

### ToDo (executed TDD-first this session)

- [x] **S73-1 (M-1, money integrity)** City-tier shipping is client-trusted:
      `shippingMethodForCity` had NO server-side caller — the checkout route,
      the Stripe mint, and the webhook all trusted the body/metadata field,
      contradicting the AGENTS.md "server re-derives it in-tx" invariant.
      Fix: the placement derives the tier IN-TX from `args.address.city`
      (`PlaceOrderArgs.shippingMethod` removed); the checkout route derives
      it for the Stripe estimate; the mint derives it for the intent amount;
      the webhook derives it from the shipping snapshot; `checkoutSchema`
      drops the field; the client stops sending it (local derivation stays
      for display only).
- [x] **S73-2 (M-2 + L-2, cart integrity)** The login cart-merge's stock
      clamp was dead code — the plan keys are `${productId}|${variant}` but
      the stock map was keyed by plain `productId`, so the S6-6 clamp never
      fired (and the inline split truncated variants containing `|`).
      Fix: a pure `stockMapForCompositeKeys` seam keys the stock map by the
      same composite keys the planner uses (unit-pinned with a
      variant-with-`|` case); `splitBulkKey` + the merge split take the
      substring after the FIRST `|`.
- [x] **S73-3 (M-3, public content)** All five legal pages carried kitchenware
      copy and a "prices are listed in US dollars" claim on a ৳ BDT store.
      Fix: the flagged paragraphs rewritten for skincare/beauty tools, BDT
      pricing, city-tiered shipping, COD-dominant payments (refunds via
      mobile financial services/bank transfer), and beauty-safety language
      (patch tests, devices) replacing the kitchen-safety section.
- [x] **S73-4 (P-1 + L-4 + I-1, nav parity + hydration)** The reference
      renders NO active-link highlight (desktop or mobile panel — measured
      live: all links `rgb(26,26,26)`, no `aria-current`); the clone
      highlighted `text-primary` via a `window.location.search` read during
      render (hydration-unsafe, audit L-4) and marked all three /shop-derived
      links active simultaneously (I-1). Fix: desktop nav drops the active
      treatment entirely (parity + kills the unsafe read); the mobile panel
      keeps `aria-current` scoped to exact-path no-query links only (the
      invisible a11y superset) and drops the color highlight; the e2e pin
      re-pinned to the new contract.

      the clone right-aligned the count in a `py-10 sm:py-14` block with a

### F-0 (CRITICAL, fixed pre-plan as S76-0): the pushed run-75 tree does not build clean

`rm -rf .next && npm run build` on the pulled 1f8aea5 tree dies in the
Turbopack PostCSS pass: `CssSyntaxError: globals.css:2:135421: Missed
semicolon`. Root cause chain (reproduced standalone + via a temporary
postcss parse-dump hook):

- Tailwind v4's automatic candidate scan reads EVERY non-gitignored text
  file in the project — **`.md` prose included**.
- The run-75 docs sweep wrote the ritual-banner class into FOUR doc files
  with a colon — `md:aspect-[3:1]` (CLAUDE.md, PAD v2.3,
  docs/session_6.md, ely-beauty_SKILL.md) — while the CODE (page.tsx:110)
  and its layout-tokens pin correctly use the slash form `md:aspect-[3/1]`.
- The scan compiled the colon-form candidate to `aspect-ratio:3:1` —
  invalid CSS — and the production build's second PostCSS parse rejects it.
- Run-75's final "build green" was a **stale-cache false-green**: the docs
  sweep ran AFTER the last real CSS compile, and Turbopack's persistent
  cache reused the pre-sweep globals.css module (the .md scan inputs are
  not tracked as compile dependencies).

**S76-0 fix (landed + verified)**: (a) `@source not` guard in globals.css —
docs/, skills/ (excluded from compilation by operator contract anyway; its
SKILL.md examples were also leaking dead rules like
`.text-\[clamp(...)\]` into the bundle), tests/, scripts/, `**/*.md`,
`**/*.mdx` never feed the candidate scan; (b) the colon typo corrected in
the four doc files (docs-truth: the code's class IS the slash form);
(c) `tests/unit/tailwind-scan-guard.test.ts` — 3 pins: the guard's presence
in source, the compiled CSS carries no colon-form aspect-ratio value (a
real compile through @tailwindcss/postcss), and the guard does not
over-exclude (.container-page + the slash-form banner pair still compile).
Verified: clean build ✓, 566/566 unit ✓, 74/74 e2e ✓.

- **A-4 (LOW, a11y)**: the overlay is not a real modal — no
  `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, and StoreChrome's shell `inert` covers
  only `cartDrawerOpen`, so Tab reaches the background while the
  full-screen sheet is open (the cart drawer has the full S13-3/S16-3
  treatment). The reference ships no dialog semantics either — this is
  the repo's "invisible a11y superset" lane, not a parity fix.

  everything) — escaping would DIVERGE from the reference, so this is
  documented-accepted parity behavior (parameterized, take:8-bounded).

### Findings feeding this cycle

**Audit 80-a (1 LOW / 3 INFO):**

- **L-1 (LOW, security posture)**: the Stripe webhook buffers the full
  body BEFORE signature verification — `await request.text()` unbounded
  at `api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:122`, on an unauthenticated, unmetered
  route (the unconfigured default 400s before any read, so the demo
  build is unaffected; a Stripe-configured deploy is exposed to
  memory-amplification DoS). The S79-7 seam's stated goal — "an
  attacker-supplied payload is never fully buffered into memory" — is
  unmet on this one path (it was outside the 9-JSON-route scope).
- I-1: npm-audit family attribution phrasing in AGENTS.md (no action).
- I-2: LIKE wildcards unescaped (documented accepted parity, unchanged).

**NEW: the reference's authoritative category model (entity API +
ID-link measurement).** The reference carries TWO parallel category
systems on every product:

- **Display categories** — a `category_ids` ARRAY (many-to-many; the
  shop pills, the home tiles, and the detail h1 filter on it):
  `Beauty Tools` = 7 products (Gua Sha, Threading Tool, Derma Roller,
  Derma Stamp, Mask Applicator, Wooden cleansing brush, Facial Ice
  Bowl), `Brush & Combs` = 3 (Sandalwood Hairbrush Oval, Exfoliating
  Gloves, Anti-cellulite Brush), `Bestsellers` = 4 (Bonnet, Pillowcase,
  Heatless Curler, **Wooden cleansing brush — a DUAL member of
  Bestsellers AND Beauty Tools**), `Gift Sets` = 0 (empty), and **6
  products belong to NO display category** (Bamboo Square, Paddle
  Oval, Bamboo Oval, Spa Socks, Crystal Hair Remover, Scalp Massager
  — they surface only under All Products).
- **Template category** — a `category` STRING field
  (`skincare` ×12, `lip_care` ×3, `body_care` ×4): the detail-page
  breadcrumb eyebrow renders it ("skincare"/"lip care", underscores →
  spaces, the eyebrow-label style), the header nav AND footer link to
  its slug filters (`?category=skincare` / `body_care` / `sets`), and
  the shop page filters on it (h1 "Shop", NO pill active, 12/4/0
  products respectively). The Category's OWN slugs (`beautytools`,
  `brush_comms`, `Bestseller`) match nothing — only IDs (display) and
  template strings filter. The 20th API product ("Pure Botanical
  Cleansing Oil") is `is_published: false` — the 19-product published
  catalog is confirmed correct.

**The deltas measured (each visible on a core page):**

- **D-81-1 — the pill result sets.** The clone's single-FK mapping
  renders beauty-tools=10 / brush-combs=6 / bestsellers=3 vs the
  reference's 7 / 3 / 4 — three extra cards under Beauty Tools
  (Spa Socks, Crystal Hair Remover, Scalp Massager), three extra
  under Brush & Combs (Bamboo Square, Paddle Oval, Bamboo Oval), and
  the cleansing brush missing from Bestsellers. The dual membership
  is unrepresentable in the single-FK schema (root cause).
- **D-81-2 — the shop h1 under a filter.** Reference: display- filter
  → the category NAME ("Beauty Tools"); template/unknown filter →
  "Shop"; unfiltered → "All Products". Clone: "All Products" always.
- **D-81-3 — the nav + footer links.** Reference nav (desktop AND
  mobile panel): Beauty Tools → `?category=skincare`, Brush & Combs →
  `?category=body_care` (template filters — the dossier's line-71
  "replicate as-observed" mapping, never replicated). Reference
  footer SHOP column: All Products / Skincare / Body Care / Gift Sets
  → `?category=skincare` / `body_care` / `sets`. Clone: its own
  display slugs everywhere.
- **D-81-4 — the detail breadcrumb eyebrow.** Reference: the template
  category ("skincare" / "lip care"). Clone: the display category
  ("Bestsellers" / "Beauty Tools").
- **D-81-5 — the one-page grid.** Reference: all 19 products on ONE
  page, no pagination controls. Clone: 12/page + a pager (2 pages).
- **D-81-6 — the shop empty state.** Reference:
  `text-center py-20` + Cormorant 24px/300 "No products found" +
  `text-sm text-muted-foreground` "Check back soon for new
  arrivals." — no border, no icon, no clear-filters link. Clone: a
  dashed box + PackageSearch icon + 18px/600 Inter + "Try adjusting
  your filters." + "Clear filters".
- **D-81-7 — the related pieces.** Reference "Complete the Ritual" =
  the 3 newest products excluding self (createdAt order — verified on
  the Bonnet AND the Pillowcase; NOT category-based). Clone:
  same-category products (count varies; 2 cards for the Bonnet).
- **D-81-8 — the ritual banner CTA.** Reference "Discover Sets" →

**Audit 81-a findings folded in:** L-1 the webhook's bare
`JSON.parse(meta.shipping)` can misclassify corrupted metadata as a

three admin dialogs import it; the track-order "sequential" comment
contradicts the ELY- crypto-random order numbers; the rate-limit
"rejected requests do not extend the count" wording is wrong); L-3
the `readBodyTextBounded` no-stream fallback caps on UTF-16 units,
not bytes.

### Findings feeding this cycle

**D-83-1 (HIGH, test infrastructure) — the e2e concurrency flake class,
reproduced and root-caused.** Observed twice this session (2 failures ×
2 of 6 full-suite runs; both victims passing in isolation and on the
following runs): `admin.spec.ts:49` (S81-11, dialog not found after the
Edit click while the `?q=Gua+Sha` navigation was still in flight) +
`storefront.spec.ts:68` (bestsellers "4 products" — seeing S81-11's
mid-test window); and `admin.spec.ts:93` (S82-3) +
`storefront.spec.ts:132` (skincare "12 products" — S82-3's
template-clear window). Three failure modes, all verified by audit 83-a:

1. **The ungated post-search Edit click.** The admin products search is
   a native GET form; `search.press("Enter")` navigates, and the very
   next statement clicks the Edit button — a client island whose
   onClick needs the NEW document's hydration. The click lands on the
   old document (torn down) or the new one pre-hydration (a no-op) →
   `expect(dialog).toBeVisible()` times out → the test aborts MID-MUTATION.
2. **Observable mutation windows.** S81-11 holds bestsellers at 5 (the
   Gua Sha's added dual membership) and S82-3 holds skincare at 11 (the
   cleared template category) for the seconds each test spends
   navigating the public storefront to verify its edit — windows any
   parallel worker's count assertion can land inside
   (`fullyParallel: true` runs admin.spec.ts inside desktop-chromium).
3. **The same-product clobber.** S81-11 and S82-3 both full-row-upsert
   the SAME Gua Sha through `upsertProductAction` (the action always
   writes `templateCategory` AND rebuilds the membership junction from
   the dialog's snapshot) — running concurrently, each save silently
   reverts the other's axis from its stale snapshot.

An aborted revert leaves the membership/template dirty for the rest of
the run AND for subsequent runs against a reused server (the
`restore-demo-stock.ts` backstop only runs at webServer start — CI's
`workers: 1` masks the whole class, which is why it surfaced on local
multi-worker runs only).

**Audit 83-a findings folded in:**

- **F-2 (LOW)**: `/admin/analytics` reads `categories[0]` through its
  own inline unordered select (`analytics/page.tsx:71,84`) — the
  S82-4 determinism fix never reached this surface, and the
  `products.ts:137` comment claims analytics attribution flows through
  `firstCategoryName` (it does not).
- **F-3 (INFO) + the USD/US remnant sweep**: the dead
  `parsed.data.country || "United States"` fallback in the addresses
  POST (`api/addresses/route.ts:63` — the Zod default "Bangladesh"
  always wins); the same dead US fallback in the account order-history
  snapshot display (`account/page.tsx:395`); and the `"$0.00"` AOV
  zero-state literal beside a ৳ formatter (`analytics/page.tsx:103`) —
  HomeNest heritage remnants (the reference has no admin/account
  surfaces to contradict).

**The reference (re-measured this session):** the mobile panel rows
89/125/161/197/233 @390×844 (36px rhythm, 14px/1.4px uppercase), the
panel ending at ABOUT, toggle-close, SEARCH-row → overlay, route-change

## Session 87 — The Lost-Config Build-Resilience Cycle (the operator's 312-error wall)

Evidence base (all verified this session):

- `docs/build_error.txt` (the operator's environment, Next 16.4.5 Turbopack):
  15 `@apply`/`@utility` "Unknown at rule" warnings + **312 module-not-found
  errors** — 311 `@/`-alias imports + 1 `tw-animate-css` (from the globals.css
  `@import`).
- The repo itself is healthy: fresh full clone → lint ✓ · typecheck ✓ ·
  typecheck:tests ✓ · 717/717 unit ✓ · build ✓ (audit 87-a: 12/12 anchors
  PASS, zero run-86 regressions, `.env.example` 9/9).
- **Scenario matrix (local reproduction, /tmp/scen)**: minus `tsconfig.json`
  → 311 `@/` errors (the operator's error block, exact); minus
  `postcss.config.mjs` → the @apply/@utility warnings + the tw-animate-css
  module-not-found; minus **both** → 15 warnings + **312 errors** — the
  operator's log reproduced signature-for-signature. Full tree: green.
- Root cause: the operator's checkout **lost `tsconfig.json` and
  `postcss.config.mjs`** — the only two build-critical root configs untouched
  since the 2026-10-12 initial migration (`87cfa40`); the files modified
  recently (package.json, next.config.ts, src/**) all survived. Their tree
  materialization drops long-untouched files.
- Why each symptom follows: no tsconfig.json → no `@/*` paths for Turbopack
  (and the build's type-check falls to TS-default resolution); no
  postcss.config.mjs → `@tailwindcss/postcss` never registers → raw PostCSS
  warns on every `@apply`/`@utility` and the plugin-resolved
  `@import "tw-animate-css"` falls to Turbopack's bare-specifier CSS
  resolution → module-not-found.
- Ruled out: `npm ci --omit=dev` (different signature — one hard "Cannot find
  module '@tailwindcss/postcss'" and typescript stays installed via prisma);
  the Next 16.4.5 workspace-marker root inference (our `outputFileTracingRoot`
  pin holds it; the operator's log shows no root warnings; the
  missing-config trees reproduce the exact signature).

The fix must therefore live in files that demonstrably survive the operator's
materialization (package.json, next.config.ts) and restore the rest:

- [x] **S87-1 (the compilation belt)**: `turbopack.resolveAlias` pin in
      `next.config.ts` — `"@/*": "./src/*"`, the identical mapping to
      tsconfig's paths, so Turbopack compilation survives a lost (or
      scaffold-default) tsconfig.json. Matrix-verified: the minus-tsconfig
      tree goes 311 errors → 0 at the compilation phase.
- [x] **S87-2 (the restore path)**: `scripts/ensure-build-configs.mjs` — a
      `CONFIG_FALLBACKS` registry embedding the five 2026-10-12-vintage
      configs (`tsconfig.json`, `postcss.config.mjs`, `vitest.config.ts`,
      `tsconfig.tests.json`, `eslint.config.mjs`) + `missingConfigFiles()` +
      `ensureAll(targetDir)` — write-if-missing-or-empty, NEVER overwrites
      existing content, direct-run guarded for library import. Each canonical
      file gains a one-line S87-2 comment header naming the restore path
      (documentation + the recency hedge for the operator's loss mechanism).
- [x] **S87-3 (the chain)**: package.json — the seven gated scripts
      (`build`, `dev`, `lint`, `test`, `test:e2e`, `typecheck`,
      `typecheck:tests`) run the bootstrap first (idempotent, ~10ms, silent
      when nothing is missing).
- [x] **S87-4 (the pins)**: `tests/unit/build-config-resilience.test.ts` —
      RED-first: the S87-1 alias presence, the registry↔canonical sync
      (string equality, the drift alarm), the temp-dir restore behavior
      (all five restored, byte-exact; existing files untouched), and the
      seven-script chain presence.
- [x] **S87-5 (the acceptance matrix)**: the poison trees must build green —
      full tree (regression), minus tsconfig.json, minus postcss.config.mjs,
      and minus both (the operator's exact tree). Plus the standing gates:
      lint · typecheck · typecheck:tests · unit · build · **e2e ×2
      consecutive** · sitemap 28 · screenshots · `.env.example`.
- [x] **S87-6 (the docs sweep)**: AGENTS.md (the build-anywhere contract +
      the incident + the registry maintenance rule), this section's
      execution log, worklog Task 81, session_30.md, CLAUDE/README counts,
      PAD v2.15, ely-beauty_SKILL.md v2.15.0 + the Appendix B entry.

Out of scope (recorded): the dev-only npm-audit families (run-86 deferred);
the a11y supersets (S79-4 ring, state-aware toggle label, Link overlay rows);
the internal `*Dollars` heritage names; the wishlist route's fixed message;
moving build toolchain (tailwindcss/@tailwindcss/postcss/tw-animate-css)
from devDependencies to dependencies — the operator's failure is the lost

**Evidence base:** the operator's standing instruction refreshed the
workspace (`git pull` at `913c872` = run-92 code `2ec891b` + the raw
narrative `docs/session_41.md`). No NEW operator-side signal artifact this

intact, `.env` with `DATABASE_URL="file:../db/custom.db"` + AUTH_SECRET,
`db/` at the repo root with the shadow converged via hardlink — same
inode). `npm install` → 0 vulnerabilities; fresh reseed (`db:setup` → 19
products / 2 users / 3 coupons / 4 categories / 11 settings).

**Baseline gates on the pulled tree (docs matched reality):** lint ✓ ·
typecheck ✓ · typecheck:tests ✓ · **749/749 unit** (65 files) ✓.

**Audit 93-a** (read-only subagent, `skills/` excluded, web-application +
code-review-checklist methodology): **12/12 standing anchors PASS ·
R1–R8 (run-92 regression surface) PASS · 0 CRITICAL — 1 MEDIUM + 3 LOW +
4 INFO.**

**The findings mapped to this plan:**

- **MEDIUM-1:** `changePasswordAction`'s rotation is THREE independent
  awaited writes (`db.user.update` → `db.session.deleteMany` →
  `createSession`) — a crash or SQLite write-lock timeout between the
  first two leaves the password CHANGED while every pre-change session
  stays alive (the exact threat the rotation exists to kill) for up to
  the 30-day TTL, with no forgot-password flow to recover. → **S93-1**
  (the transactional rotation seam, the S13-4 `growReviewAggregate`
  precedent).
- **LOW-1:** the S92-2a credential single-sourcing missed
  `scripts/capture-screenshots.mjs` — three login sites + a track-order
  URL still hardcode both pairs. → **S93-2** (the script converts to
  TypeScript and imports `demo-credentials.ts`; invocation becomes
  `npx tsx`, the `restore-demo-stock.ts` pattern).
- **LOW-2:** `ely-beauty_SKILL.md`'s demo-account table still carries the
  pre-rename `@homenestkitchen.com` emails (stale since run 72;
  contradicts `demo-credentials.ts`, AGENTS.md, README). → **S93-3**.
- **LOW-3:** the S92-2e advisory detector burns a synchronous scrypt
  (~30–80 ms event-loop stall) on EVERY production dashboard render —
  including the post-rotation steady state. → **S93-4** (TTL-cached
  negative verdict; positives never cached so the advisory clears the
  moment the password rotates).
- INFO-1 (no-JS fallback of the account forms GETs the current URL with
  the fields in the query — the pre-existing ProfileForm pattern, login/
  register degrade to POSTs via useActionState; recorded, no action) ·
  INFO-2 (`newPassword === currentPassword` allowed — cryptographically
  harmless, rotation still fires; recorded) · INFO-3 (a scheme-less
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` still throws in `new URL` — fail-fast is the
  documented posture; recorded) · INFO-4 (docs count lockstep verified
  current repo-wide — 749/92/28/25/9 all exact).

Widening an existing net means asking, for every dimension the grammar pins (lower bound, upper bound, capture class), whether BOTH sides of that dimension are now owned — and probing the widened grammar against the live corpus BEFORE writing the pins, because the corpus may carry legitimate material (a closed-sub-series cite) in exactly the shape the widened grammar flags; the move is the run-101 precedent: rephrase the legitimate material to a shape the grammar cannot read as the claim, and keep the canonical literal matching so the net stays non-vacuous.

**Lessons for the next cycle:** the run-103 lesson ("a shape has TWO sides") has a third face the audits keep finding one run late: a grammar's INVARIANT COMMENT can outlive the grammar's actual behavior — the `.md` lookahead's exclusion claim was documented, pinned by a pin that never tested it, and false as written for three whole runs (the exclusion only ever worked by luck of no live material, and even then it mangled what it caught). When a grammar ships with an exclusion invariant (a lookahead, a boundary rule), the pin that proves it must feed the grammar the EXCLUDED shape and assert both the clean exclusion AND the un-mangled match text — an invariant nobody probes is a claim nobody checked; and backtracking is a standing witness that a regex's documented intent and its operational semantics are two different artifacts, to be reconciled by probe, not by comment.

When a new money DOMAIN joins a codebase (a second currency, a different minor unit), the seam that renders it needs its own named formatter with its own pins — and an audit that re-derives expected values from the DOMAIN (what currency IS this number?) rather than from the existing pins (what does the current code print?) is the only probe that catches the class; the pinned fixtures of a defect are its best camouflage.

- **HIGH-1 (F-1, the cycle's centerpiece):** **the customer-facing Stripe Pay button renders the USD intent amount through the ৳ formatter — the S105-1 class surviving on the charge-consent surface.** The mint route converts the server-derived poisha total through `stripeChargeAmount` and echoes `intent.amount` — **USD minor units** (`currency: "usd"`) — which the island stores and passes to `CardPaymentPanel`, whose button renders `Pay — ${formatMoney(amount)}` (the BDT poisha formatter). With `STRIPE_BDT_PER_USD=120`, a ৳288 order mints a $2.40 intent → the button reads **"Pay — ৳2.40"** while the card is charged **$2.40** (≈৳288) — wrong currency symbol AND a magnitude ~120× below the ৳288 total shown in the same flow's review block. Display-only (the charge amount, order books, and receipts all ride server truth), but on the charge-consent surface. The run-105 change-set asserted the button "stays ৳ — the BDT cart total"; that premise was **false** — the echoed value is the converted USD intent amount, not `money.total`. No pin covered it (the island never mounts in test envs — Stripe unconfigured — so 830/830 stayed green through the mislabel). Adopted as S106-1.
- **INFO-1 (F-2):** the mint route's `PaymentIntentSession.amount` docblock names neither currency nor units ("Echoed for the island's own amount display") — the ambiguity that enabled HIGH-1. Remediated in S106-1 (the docblock names the domain: USD minor units, render with `formatStripeUsd`, never `formatMoney`).
- **INFO-2 (F-3, no-action):** `formatOverlayPrice` and `formatStripeUsd` have byte-identical bodies across disjoint domains (the S82-1 overlay USD-template quirk on BDT values vs true USD minor units) — deliberate per the domain-separation doctrine; a future "DRY" merge would re-blur the domains; the docblocks are the defense. Recorded here so future audits do not re-derive it as novel.

**Design (the fix shape):** the domain-correct, surgical fix — the Pay button renders the echoed amount through `formatStripeUsd` (`Pay — $2.40`), the S105-1 formatter extended to the charge-consent surface (the review block's ৳ totals are the parent's children — the BDT surface; the card's charge is USD, and the button says exactly what the card will be charged). The island's `formatMoney` import drops entirely (no BDT money surface remains in the file); the mint route's session docblock names the domain; `money.ts`'s `formatStripeUsd` docblock and `money.test.ts`'s S105-1 describe comment re-word their stale "Pay button stays ৳" claims (live-tense comments carrying the run-105 mis-assessment). Source pins (the S82-1 precedent — the island cannot mount in test envs): the button composes `formatStripeUsd(amount)`, the island source carries no `formatMoney`, and the route docblock names the USD-minor-unit domain.

- **F-1 (HIGH, adopted as S109-1 + S109-3, the cycle's centerpiece):** **the production `AUTH_SECRET` is committed in a publicly readable repo** — `docs/start_server_log.txt:8`, inside the operator's own deployment-log artifact (a captured `diff .env .env.example` from the production deploy at `https://ely-beauty.jesspete.shop`, present in every one of the file's 9 commits since `36e85de`). The value is a 32-byte base64 secret (the `.env` side of the diff), NOT the sandbox dev secret — verified distinct by hash comparison. The repo is publicly readable (unauthenticated clone verified). The key is load-bearing in two places: the session-cookie HMAC (defense-in-depth) and — critically — the **deterministic** order-receipt capability token (`orderAccessToken` = HMAC-SHA256(AUTH_SECRET, "order-access:"+orderNumber), `src/lib/order-access.ts:27-32`), whose timing-safe verification is the **sole** gate on `/checkout/success` rendering the buyer's receipt (email, phone, full shipping address, items, spend). Anyone who can read the repo can compute a valid receipt token for any *known* `ELY-XXXXXXXX` order number → targeted PII disclosure per order; full-session forgery additionally requires a DB-backed 256-bit token (no direct admin takeover), and blind enumeration of the 36^8 space is impractical — HIGH, not CRITICAL, matching the run-92 calibration for targeted-exploit findings. **Why 107 prior audits missed it:** the standing secrets sweep greps fixed MARKERS (operator email/password literals, 64-hex, sk_live, OPENSSH, ghp_, AKIA) — a base64 `AUTH_SECRET` value matches none of them; run-92 even quoted the file's "a real AUTH_SECRET" line and classified it as an operator signal artifact, not a leak surface. The class: **secrets leak in SHAPES, and the sweep only ever banned MARKERS** — the run-108 lesson ("a class deserves a net at every stratum its residue can reach") recurring at the OPERATOR-LOG stratum, the one stratum no net had ever covered (the operator's own committed artifacts).
- **F-2 (LOW, adopted as S109-2):** **the reference-site operator credentials sit in the four vendored founding prompts** — `docs/prompt-to-create.md:2`, `docs/prompt-to-review.md:4`, `docs/prompt-to-review-2.md:6`, `docs/prompt-to-review-3.md:6` each quote the base44 reference-site login verbatim (ID + a `$`-prefixed 8-char password, backtick-wrapped). The repo is public → anyone can log into the operator's reference site. Not app credentials (the app's seeded defaults are the documented `Admin123!`/`Demo1234!`, server-side only). The founding prompts are historical documents — but a live credential pair in a public repo is a leak, not history (the S108-2 code-wins rule at the security stratum).
- **INFO-1 (no-action, recorded):** the `orderAccessToken` deterministic-HMAC design itself is standard capability-token practice (GitHub-style signed URLs); the defect was the COMMIT of the key, not the derivation. A leak-resistant redesign (random per-order token persisted on the row) would require a schema migration + touching the checkout/success seam for defense-in-depth against a key leak whose real fix is rotation — recorded as a considered alternative, not adopted this cycle.
- **INFO-2 (no-action, frozen history):** `docs/REMEDIATION_PLAN.md` names the operator identity (`sepnetflix2023`, no password) at four execution-log sites — identity, not a credential pair; the frozen-history exemption is load-bearing.

**Design (the fix shape):** two redactions + one shape net + one operator advisory. The redactions: `docs/start_server_log.txt:8`'s value → a placeholder (the diff structure preserved); the four founding prompts' password literal → a placeholder (the ID stays — identity is already public in the frozen history; the PAIR is the secret). The net (the countermeasure, per the S108 lesson): the secrets sweep moves from MARKERS to SHAPES — `docs-counts.test.ts` gains the S109 describe with two pins scanning every tracked text file (the S99-1 filesystem-derivation convention, `skills/` excluded per the standing instruction): **S109-1a** no value-shaped `AUTH_SECRET` assignment anywhere (`AUTH_SECRET\s*=\s*["'`]?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{16,}` — base64/hex value shapes at `openssl rand` lengths; `.env.example`'s empty `""` and prose mentions of the NAME pass; the property-passing shapes in src/tests (`AUTH_SECRET: …`) are outside the assignment shape); **S109-2a** no `$`-prefixed password credential anywhere (`password\s+`?\$[A-Za-z0-9]{6,}` — the founding prompts' shape, backtick-optional). The pins ban the SHAPES, never the values — the net carries no toxin (the S108-2a paraphrase discipline generalized to the secrets class: a secrets net that quotes the secret it bans would itself be a leak). **The advisory (the real fix):** the in-repo redaction does NOT purge git history — the value remains retrievable from every prior commit; the complete fix is rotating `AUTH_SECRET` at the production deploy (a new `openssl rand -base64 32` value + redeploy; all sessions invalidate, users re-login), and the operator's log-capture ritual must redact before committing future `start_server_log` refreshes (the S109-1a pin now catches a re-leak by name at the next cycle's gate).

**Lessons for the next cycle:** the run-108 lesson ("a remediation class deserves a net at every stratum its residue can reach") recurs at the deepest stratum yet — the OPERATOR's OWN ARTIFACTS: `start_server_log.txt` is operator-generated, operator-committed content that no code review ever gates, and it carried the highest-value secret in the system across 107 audits because the secrets sweep was built on MARKERS (fixed strings to grep) while secrets actually leak in SHAPES (value-shaped assignments that match no marker). The countermeasure is the shape net (S109-1a/2a) — and its two design rules generalize: (1) a secrets net must ban the SHAPE, never quote the value (a net carrying the toxin it bans is itself a leak — the S108-2a paraphrase discipline at the security stratum); (2) the corpus floor guards the walk (a broken enumeration passing vacuously is the S104-1 over-scoping class inverted — the net must prove it SCANNED, not just that it found nothing). Also: the in-repo redaction is the HALF-fix for any committed secret — git history retains the value forever, so the complete fix is rotation at the source, and the advisory must ride every artifact the operator reads (plan, worklog, session log, commit message, the final reply). And an environmental note for the next cycle's screenshot ritual: this sandbox generation ships no `xxd` — validate the PNG signatures with Python's struct module instead.

**Lessons for the next cycle:** (1) the S109 net's first live interception proves the MARKERS→SHAPES doctrine — but the recurring stratum is now precise: **the operator's raw narratives quote the standing instruction verbatim, credentials included** — every raw-narrative commit is a potential re-leak, and the next shape evolution (if one is ever needed) should assume the leak arrives in arbitrary phrasing (the S110 non-adjacency net is the first step; the corpus scope boundary at `skills/` stays a hand-remediated stratum, recorded in the describe comment). (2) A secrets net must be designed against ITS OWN SOURCE: the corpus pin scanning the test file that carries the grammar fixtures is a self-referential trap — concatenate the fixtures so the banned shape never appears contiguously in source, and never solve it with a self-exclusion (a blind spot is worse than a trap). (3) The parity discipline's standing rule re-proven: a claim of "exactly like the reference" is only as good as the measurement that made it — the S77-2 panel-stays-open claim survived 33 cycles because `panelStateAfterOverlay` was only ever probe-side; every interaction STATE, not just geometry, needs both-sides measurement. (4) The environmental recurring note: the capture script and the server must share ONE bash invocation (the sandbox kills the server between invocations — the shot-23 failure was exactly the session-44 class).
